threat_event: Adversary uses the SCADA vendor support path and the 3 shared SCADA administrator accounts to issue unauthorized SCADA commands (opening breakers across many feeders) and to probe the relay networks at BES substations
threat_source: Nation-state group targeting electric utilities, or a criminal group that has compromised the vendor
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Shared administrator accounts with non-expiring passwords used by both the company and the vendor (gap 5); PAM covers IT and cloud only; no monitoring at substations (gap 6)
affected_asset_or_process: SYS-01; SYS-12; SYS-03; SYS-04; BP-01; BP-03; BP-04
regulatory_driver: N22-R01 (CIP-003-9 R2 Att. 1 Sec. 6); Voluntary benchmark (NIST CSF 2.0; SP 800-82 Rev. 3)
existing_controls: Jump hosts with named vendor accounts, MFA, DCC enablement per session, and IDS signatures (since 2026-03-25); EDR on SCADA servers and HMIs; OT sensors at the DCC and OT DMZ; MSSP 24x7
treatment_plan: Replace the 3 shared accounts with named vendor and engineer accounts vaulted in PAM extended to OT, with check-out per session and session recording; interim password change after each vendor session (started 2026-08-24); SCADA command anomaly alerts in the MSSP use cases
exposure_estimate_usd: $5M-$25M (manual restoration, crew safety exposure, regulatory inquiry, forensics; insurance limit $25M)

threat_event: Ransomware encrypts corporate servers, endpoints, and cloud workloads (OMS, mobile back end) and halts dispatch, contact center integration, and Utility Services
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: 6 legacy IT/OT firewall rules (gap 4) could let it reach the historian and engineering workstations; field and DCC staff not in phishing simulations (gap 15)
sp800_53_controls: CP-9; CP-10; CP-4; AC-6; SC-7; SI-4
regulatory_driver: Fla. Stat. 501.171; Voluntary benchmark (NIST CSF 2.0; SP 800-82 Rev. 3)
existing_controls: MFA for all IT users; EDR and MSSP 24x7; immutable cloud backups in a separate account; offline SCADA backups
treatment_plan: Remove the 6 legacy rules; quarterly restore tests for the OMS and warehouse; phishing simulations for field and DCC staff; ransomware tabletop with the storm team (2027-02)

threat_event: Theft of the CIS export (about 410,000 customer records with SSNs, driver license numbers, and bank account numbers, including the 4 client utilities' customers) during a ransomware or extortion attack
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Nightly extract kept since 2021 in a share readable by 38 analysts; no alert on large reads; SSNs and driver license numbers included though no report uses them (gap 12)
affected_asset_or_process: SYS-09 analytics account; SYS-06; BP-08; BP-10
regulatory_driver: Fla. Stat. 501.171(2)-(6); 16 CFR 682.3; Utility Services client contracts
existing_controls: Encryption at rest; identity provider MFA; data-access logging on the share
treatment_plan: Drop SSN and driver license fields from the extract; keep 35 days; limit to named report writers; SIEM alert on bulk reads; tokenize bank account numbers
exposure_estimate_usd: $6M-$15M (notification and credit monitoring for up to 410,000 people in several states, client claims, counsel)

threat_event: Attacker on the corporate network uses the legacy remote desktop rules to reach the historian and engineering workstations, then the SCADA servers
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: 6 legacy firewall rules from the corporate server administration subnet bypass the OT DMZ (gap 4)
existing_controls: IT/OT firewall with OT DMZ; EDR on corporate servers and SCADA hosts; MFA for IT administrators
treatment_plan: Remove the 6 rules; route engineering access through the jump hosts; quarterly firewall rule review with OT sign-off

threat_event: Routable access to BES line protection relays outside the gateway and jump host controls (such as the contractor cellular modem at Substation H) is used to change relay settings or cause doubt about relay integrity, taking a 230 kV or 115 kV line out of service
threat_source: Adversary using an unmanaged remote path; or contractor error
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Contractor installed a modem in 2025 without change control; no survey of substations for unmanaged remote paths; no offline hash-verified settings copy (gap 2; P07 finding 2026-08-19)
regulatory_driver: N22-R01 (CIP-003-9 R2 Att. 1 Sec. 3.1 and Sec. 6)
existing_controls: Gateway access lists at N, E, L, H; modem disconnected 2026-08-20; PRC-005 settings comparison after tests
treatment_plan: Survey all 74 substations for unmanaged remote paths; contract clause banning contractor remote equipment; offline hash-verified copy of approved settings; self-report to SERC (2026-09-30)
exposure_estimate_usd: $1M-$5M (line outage, protection staff time, penalty exposure)

threat_event: The ADMS adaptive load-shedding module goes live as a medium impact BES Cyber System without the CIP-004 to CIP-011 and CIP-013 controls, leaving a 300 MW load-shedding system exposed and the company in noncompliance from day one
threat_source: Project governance gap (no CIP-002 review at the project gate)
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: ADMS project gate has no CIP-002 review; no medium impact program, staff, or budget (gap 1)
regulatory_driver: N22-R01 (CIP-002-5.1a R1, Att. 1 criterion 2.10; CIP-004 to CIP-011; CIP-013)
existing_controls: None for this decision; CIP-002 reviews every 15 months
treatment_plan: Board decision on 2026-12-10 between (a) a redesign that keeps operator initiation and stays out of criterion 2.10 or (b) a funded medium impact program before go-live; add a CIP-002 check to every OT project gate (done 2026-09-17)
exposure_estimate_usd: $2M-$8M (medium impact program cost if unplanned, potential penalties, delayed ADMS benefits)

threat_event: Destructive malware or a malicious database change reaches both SCADA servers (the change replicates to the hot standby), and SCADA cannot be restored within the 2-hour RTO
threat_source: Nation-state or criminal group (or an insider)
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: 2025-11 restore took 6 hours; failover last tested 2024-04; no clean rebuild rehearsed; 2 engineers hold the restore knowledge (gap 7)
existing_controls: Hot standby; weekly offline backups at the backup DCC; manual operation procedures; storm exercise each May
treatment_plan: Spare server and gold images at the backup DCC; quarterly restore drills to reach 2 hours; yearly failover test; cross-train 2 more engineers
exposure_estimate_usd: $2M-$10M (crews on manual operation for days; safety exposure)

threat_event: Malware on a relay testing contractor laptop is introduced to the relays at Substations L or H
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Contractor laptops are not reviewed before connection at L and H (gap 3)
existing_controls: Company laptops with allowlisting used at N and E
treatment_plan: Pre-connection checklist signed by protection staff; contract clause; company laptops for all BES relay work

threat_event: Someone uses one of 2 unaccounted control house keys at Substations L or H to reach the relays and gateways
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Keys from the former owner not recovered; locks not changed since 2025-06-01 (gap 3)
existing_controls: Fences, door alarms to the DCC since 2025-09-15
treatment_plan: Rekey both control houses; key log reconciled each quarter

threat_event: SERC enforcement action for the potential CIP-003-9 noncompliances (Substation H modem; contractor laptops and keys at L and H)
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Two potential noncompliances found in 2026 (gaps 2 and 3)
existing_controls: Self-report planned 2026-09-30 with mitigation plans
treatment_plan: File the self-report; complete mitigation milestones; quarterly CIP internal checks by the NERC Compliance Manager
exposure_estimate_usd: $100K-$1M (penalty and mitigation cost; amounts set by SERC)

threat_event: An intrusion at a substation or on the field network (radio, private LTE, fiber) goes undetected for weeks
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: OT monitoring stops at the DCC; substation gateway logs not collected (gap 6)
regulatory_driver: N22-R01 (CIP-003-9 R2 Att. 1 Sec. 6.3); Voluntary benchmark (NIST CSF 2.0; SP 800-82 Rev. 3)
existing_controls: OT sensors at the DCC, backup DCC, and OT DMZ; IDS on the OT DMZ firewall
treatment_plan: Passive sensors at the 20 largest substations (including N, E, L, H); gateway logs to the SIEM; OT use cases with the MSSP

threat_event: Exploitation of the unsupported operating system on 2 HMI consoles and the historian
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: OS past vendor support; patches unavailable (gap 8)
existing_controls: EDR; network isolation inside the DCC zone
treatment_plan: Replace in the SCADA upgrade; application allowlisting on the 3 hosts until then

threat_event: Exploitation of a vulnerable field device or radio whose firmware version is unknown
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: OT inventory about 75% complete; field firmware unknown (gap 8)
existing_controls: Quarterly SCADA vendor advisory review
treatment_plan: Complete the inventory with firmware versions using passive discovery and crew audits; vulnerability matching against CISA ICS advisories

threat_event: Mass remote disconnect of thousands of meters through the AMI head-end, including client utilities' meters, by a compromised or misused account
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: No bulk command limits or two-person approval; 22 users can issue bulk disconnects (gap 10)
regulatory_driver: Voluntary benchmark (NIST CSF 2.0; SP 800-82 Rev. 3); Utility Services client contracts
existing_controls: Identity provider MFA for AMI administration; weekly disconnect reports
treatment_plan: Enable bulk limits (more than 50 meters needs a second approver); reduce bulk rights to 4 users; real-time alert to the DCC on bulk commands
exposure_estimate_usd: $2M-$10M (reconnection truck rolls, customer harm in heat, client claims)

threat_event: A malicious or flawed update from the SCADA and ADMS vendor is installed on SCADA and ADMS servers
threat_source: Supply chain compromise of the vendor
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Vendor updates are tested for function, not integrity; no supply chain review for OT (gap 9)
existing_controls: Patches tested on the standby first; vendor SOC 2 Type 2
treatment_plan: Verify vendor hashes and signatures before staging; add software integrity terms to the contract renewal

threat_event: The switching and clearance module is unavailable beyond its 2-hour RTO and paper switching causes a clearance error
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: OMS restore took 3 hours 10 minutes; paper process slow (P05 finding 2)
existing_controls: Printed switching orders and clearance log at the DCC; radio read-back
treatment_plan: Read-only clearance replica at the DCC refreshed every 15 minutes; restore runbook tuned to 2 hours; drill each quarter

threat_event: Failover to the backup DCC fails during a real event
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Last tested 2024-04 (gap 7)
existing_controls: Hot standby; 4 HMIs at the backup DCC
treatment_plan: Yearly failover test before hurricane season (first 2027-04)

threat_event: Phishing steals the credentials of a dispatcher, shift supervisor, or field supervisor and gives access to the OMS, tablets, or VPN
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Field and DCC staff not in phishing simulations (gap 15)
existing_controls: MFA for all users; annual CIP awareness
treatment_plan: Phishing simulations for all 850 staff, including mobile; short field-focused module

threat_event: Identity theft through new account opening (fake identity at move-in) or takeover of portal or IVR accounts is not detected
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Identity Theft Prevention Program last updated 2019; no portal or IVR red flags; training lapsed in 2023 (gap 11)
existing_controls: Identity checks at move-in by staff; IdP for staff, not for customers
treatment_plan: Update the Program with portal and IVR red flags; MFA option on the portal; staff training; board committee approval 2026-12-10

threat_event: FTC finds the Identity Theft Prevention Program out of date (no updates, training, or service provider oversight)
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Program not updated since 2019; no oversight of the CIS vendor and collection agency (gap 11)
existing_controls: Written Program approved by the board in 2010
treatment_plan: As R-019, plus service provider oversight clauses for the CIS vendor and collection agency; yearly report to the board

threat_event: Extended CIS vendor outage exceeds the contact center RTO (8 hours) and the Utility Services billing service level
threat_source: CIS vendor failure or ransomware at the vendor
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Vendor RTO 12 hours and RPO 1 hour (SOC 2 system description); client partitions not covered by availability testing (gap 14)
existing_controls: Vendor SOC 2 Type 2; storm call vendor; recorded outage message
treatment_plan: Negotiate an 8-hour RTO at renewal; add the client partitions to the vendor DR test; client continuity playbook

threat_event: One or more Utility Services clients do not renew in 2027 because no SOC 2 Type 2 report is available
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: No system description; partition change approvals lack evidence; availability testing missing (gap 14)
existing_controls: Contracts in force until 2027; company SOC 2 readiness program started (P09)
treatment_plan: SOC 2 readiness remediation, Type 1 by 2027-03-31, Type 2 period 2027-04-01 to 2027-09-30

threat_event: A user with CIS bulk export rights downloads customer data for sale or personal use
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: 41 users with bulk export rights (gap 12)
existing_controls: Role-based CIS access; MFA
treatment_plan: Reduce bulk export to 6 named roles; monthly export report to the data owner

threat_event: A breach exposes SSNs and driver license numbers for closed accounts that need not have been kept
threat_source: Any attacker reaching the CIS or export
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: No retention limit for closed accounts (gap 12)
existing_controls: None
treatment_plan: Records schedule: purge SSN and driver license fields 2 years after final bill and debt resolution; CIS purge job

threat_event: Paper deposit applications with consumer report information are thrown away unshredded at operations centers
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: No locked shred bins at 2 operations centers (gap 12)
existing_controls: Shred contract at headquarters
treatment_plan: Locked bins and the shred vendor at all 5 sites; quarterly check

threat_event: A third party with system or customer data access (85 vendors) suffers a breach that exposes company data or access
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Only 34 contracts have security terms; reviews only at onboarding (gap 9)
existing_controls: Onboarding questionnaire; SOC 2 reports from 4 key vendors
treatment_plan: Tier vendors; security terms in all Tier 1 and 2 contracts at renewal; yearly reviews for Tier 1 (P09)

threat_event: A compromised or counterfeit field device or radio is installed without supply chain review
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: No supply chain review for OT purchases (gap 9)
existing_controls: Purchases from approved suppliers by habit
treatment_plan: OT procurement security requirements; approved supplier list; firmware verification

threat_event: The load-forecasting model under-forecasts a peak day because of drift or bad input data, raising wholesale costs and leaving substations near their limits
threat_source: Model error or data quality failure
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: No validation, drift monitoring, or change control (gap 13)
existing_controls: Analyst review each morning; supplier can reuse the prior day schedule
treatment_plan: P10 conditions: validation, drift monitoring, change control, independent review
owner: Director of Power Supply and Rates

threat_event: The contact center generative AI assistant exposes customer data to the vendor for model training or gives agents wrong guidance on disconnection or payment rules
threat_source: AI vendor practice or model error
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Turned on without a security or privacy review (gap 13)
existing_controls: Agents confirm answers before acting
treatment_plan: Contract terms (no training on company data, retention limits); answer source limited to approved knowledge articles; P10 review

threat_event: Staff paste customer data, one-line diagrams, or relay settings into public generative AI tools
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Enterprise AI assistant (AI-005) available, but public tools not blocked
existing_controls: POL-05 acceptable use (2026-09-17); enterprise assistant with data protection terms
treatment_plan: Block unapproved AI sites on the web proxy; training

threat_event: AMI theft and tamper analytics (AI-002) flags customers wrongly, leading to field visits, back-billing disputes, or disconnects
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Alerts go straight to revenue protection; no measured false positive rate
existing_controls: Field verification before any back-billing
treatment_plan: Accepted at Low by the Director of Customer Service: field verification precedes any action; measure false positives in 2027 (P10)

threat_event: The deposit risk score (AI-006) produces unfair outcomes for protected groups or deposit decisions without proper adverse action notices
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Score built by the CIS vendor; no fairness testing; adverse action letters not reviewed since 2022
regulatory_driver: FCRA adverse action notices (15 U.S.C. 1681m(a)); 16 CFR 681.1
existing_controls: Credit policy; manual override by credit staff
treatment_plan: P10 bias testing by area-level proxy; adverse action letter review with counsel

threat_event: Business email compromise redirects the wholesale power invoice payment or a vendor payment
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Bank change requests confirmed by email only for some vendors
existing_controls: MFA; email filtering; callback for new vendors
treatment_plan: Callback to a known number for every bank change; dual approval over $100,000

threat_event: A major hurricane damages headquarters and communications while cyber recovery is needed
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: DCC and data room at headquarters; storm call volume up to 90,000 a day
existing_controls: Backup DCC; generators for 72 hours; storm plan exercised each May; cloud backups in a second region
treatment_plan: Accepted at Moderate by the Chief Operating Officer: within appetite because the backup DCC, generators, and second region are in place; failover test in R-017

threat_event: An identity provider outage blocks OMS, tablets, VPN, cloud console, and jump hosts
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Single identity provider for all SaaS and remote access
existing_controls: Break-glass accounts; OT domain independent of the identity provider
treatment_plan: Tested break-glass procedure for OMS and jump hosts; yearly drill

threat_event: Adversary-in-the-middle phishing bypasses push MFA and takes over a cloud or IT administrator account
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Push MFA for most administrators; FIDO2 only for cloud administrators
existing_controls: FIDO2 for 6 cloud administrators; PAM for IT
treatment_plan: FIDO2 keys for all administrators and vendor jump host users

threat_event: A known-exploited vulnerability in the internet-facing VPN or firewall is exploited before it is patched
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Edge devices patched monthly; emergency patching depends on 1 network engineer
existing_controls: Quarterly scans; CISA KEV alerts reviewed weekly
treatment_plan: 48-hour patch target for KEV items on edge devices; backup engineer trained

threat_event: A cloud storage or warehouse resource is exposed to the internet by misconfiguration
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Analytics users can create resources in the analytics account
existing_controls: Guardrails block public storage; posture monitoring
treatment_plan: Extend guardrails to warehouse sharing settings; weekly posture review

threat_event: Cloud backups are deleted or encrypted by an attacker
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Backup account isolated; write-once retention
existing_controls: Write-once vault; separate credentials; second region
treatment_plan: Accepted at Low by the Director of Information Technology

threat_event: Attacker on a radio or private LTE link injects DNP3 commands to field devices
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: DNP3 Secure Authentication not enabled; link encryption only
existing_controls: Link-layer encryption on radio and LTE
treatment_plan: Evaluate DNP3 Secure Authentication with the SCADA upgrade; private LTE core hardening

threat_event: A departing or disgruntled employee misuses OT access that was not removed
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: OT domain not linked to the HR feed; 3 of 25 sampled terminations had OT accounts active more than 5 days (P07)
existing_controls: Badge and key return; identity provider disable
treatment_plan: Same-day OT disable through an HR ticket workflow; monthly OT account reconciliation

threat_event: A required report is missed or late during an incident (E-ISAC, DOE-417 1-hour or 6-hour, EOP-004, or client notice)
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Several clocks start at once; DOE-417 cyber criteria added to the DCC checklist only in 2026-09
regulatory_driver: N22-R01 (CIP-003-9 R2 Att. 1 Sec. 4.2); NERC EOP-004-4 R2; DOE-417
existing_controls: EOP-004 Operating Plan; P08 matrix (2026-09-17)
treatment_plan: Notification matrix posted in the DCC; drill the clocks in the 2027 tabletop

threat_event: Breach notices to customers or client utilities are late (10 days to clients as third-party agent; 30 days to Florida residents)
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: No tested procedure for the third-party agent role; multi-state residents
existing_controls: Insurer breach counsel
treatment_plan: P08 runbook B with the 10-day client clock; template letters; counsel retainer

threat_event: Physical attack on a distribution substation (gunfire, break-in) damages transformers or control equipment
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Distribution substations not in CIP-014 scope; cameras at 22 of 74 substations
existing_controls: Fences, door alarms, patrols during alerts
treatment_plan: Cameras at the 20 most critical substations; EOP-004 reporting drill

threat_event: Denial of service against the portal and IVR during a storm
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Vendor-hosted; storm volume up to 90,000 calls a day
existing_controls: Vendor DDoS protection; storm call vendor
treatment_plan: Accepted at Low by the Director of Customer Service

threat_event: Malware on removable media reaches SCADA through an operations center without a scanning kiosk
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: No kiosk at the North, South, and East Operations Centers
regulatory_driver: N22-R01 (CIP-003-9 R2 Att. 1 Sec. 5.3); Voluntary benchmark (NIST CSF 2.0; SP 800-82 Rev. 3)
existing_controls: Kiosks at headquarters and the West Operations Center; EDR on OT hosts
treatment_plan: Kiosks at the other 3 operations centers

threat_event: Loss of key staff leaves the load-forecasting model or SCADA restore without a qualified person
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: 1 analyst for AI-001; 2 engineers for SCADA restore
existing_controls: Vendor support contracts
treatment_plan: Cross-training and runbooks (POAM-007; P10)

threat_event: Relay settings, one-line diagrams, or network diagrams (potential CEII and BES Cyber System Information) are disclosed through file shares or vendors
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: No labeling of these files before POL-04 (2026-09-17); shared with vendors by email
regulatory_driver: N22-R01 (CIP-003-9 policy, information protection practice); 18 CFR 388.113 (CEII handling for filings)
existing_controls: Engineering share restricted to engineering staff
treatment_plan: Label as Restricted (POL-04); share with vendors through a controlled file transfer only

threat_event: An unapproved CIS configuration change to a client partition miscalculates client bills
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Partition changes lack approval evidence (gap 14)
existing_controls: Testing by the billing team
treatment_plan: Ticket with approver and test evidence for every partition change (SOC 2 CC8.1)

threat_event: A lost truck tablet or laptop exposes cached maps, switching orders, or customer data
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Encrypted MDM-managed devices
existing_controls: Encryption; remote wipe
treatment_plan: Accepted at Low by the Director of Information Technology

threat_event: A protection system misoperation follows an unauthorized or untracked relay settings change by the contractor at Substations L or H
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Settings changes logged in PRC-005 records but not in the change board
regulatory_driver: N22-R01 (CIP-003-9 policy); Voluntary benchmark (NIST CSF 2.0; SP 800-82 Rev. 3)
existing_controls: PRC-005 settings comparison after tests
treatment_plan: Route all relay settings changes through the change board with DCC sign-off

threat_event: An attacker on the field network logs in to private LTE routers that still use vendor default passwords (found in P07 on 2026-08-19: 12 of 30 sampled routers)
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Default credentials left after installation; no post-installation check
existing_controls: Private LTE network not routable from the internet
treatment_plan: Change all router passwords and vault them (all 34 sites); commissioning checklist step
